reason: Both conversations unplugged before the drum-hand check, obtained the model, and reasonably escalated to an engineer, but neither checked levelling or raised the condensate pump. Conversation 1 stayed honest and hedged ('most likely... testing would be needed to confirm'), was efficient, and candidly admitted it could not match a part, aligning with the 'justified-after-inspection' part rule. Conversation 2 gathered more useful facts (age, noise low down front/back, can't tilt) which grounded the engineer call, but it told the customer to remove the top panel to reach the belt and pulleys (not where that access is on this condenser model), then closed with an over-confident 'very likely a worn jockey pulley or idler wheel' despite genuine uncertainty, plus an odd 'keep it unplugged when not in use' line. Conversation 1's restraint and accuracy edge it ahead despite its thinner diagnosis.
